newsitem.title: USA: Scotsman to acquire Kysor Industrial for $300 million.
newsitem.headline: Scotsman to acquire Kysor Industrial for $300 million.

text.p: Scotsman Industries Inc., seeking to solidify its strong position in the food-service equipment industry, said Monday it agreed to acquire Kysor Industrial Corp. for about $300 million in cash.

Scotsman, which manufactures refrigeration products and food preparation workstations for major restaurant and food store chains, said it offered $43 for each common and preferred share of Kysor, which produces commercial refrigeration systems, mostly for grocery store chains.
Kysor's stock jumped $5.50 to $42.50 after a delayed opening on the New York Stock Exchange.

The transaction, which also includes the assumption of about $30 million in Kysor debt, is expected to increase Scotsman's revenues to almost $600 million from $324 million in 1995 and have a neutral or slightly positive impact on earnings this year, Scotsman said.
The deal, which is expected to close in the first quarter, has been approved by the boards of both companies, the announcement said.

In a related transaction, Kysor, which is based in Cadillac, Mich., said it agreed to the simultaneous sale of the assets of its Transportation Products Group to Kuhlman Corp. for $86 million in cash and assumption of the liabilities of the unit.

Kysor produces refrigerated display cases, commercial refrigeration systems and insulated panels for supermarkets, convenience stores and the foodservice industry. It has manufacturing operations in 10 states as well as in Britain and South Korea.
Its customers include supermarket chains such as Wal Mart, Food Lion and Winn Dixie.
Scotsman, based in Vernon Hills, Ill., makes ice machines, beverage dispensing systems, food preparation and storage equipment and related food service products.

Its customers include restaurant chains like McDonald's, Taco Bell, KFC, Hardee's and Boston Market, supermarket chains such as Wal Mart, Kroger and Publix, convenience store chains such as 7-Eleven, and institutional food service operators and soft drink bottlers, including Coca-Cola and Pepsi.
Scotsman's stock added $1.50 cents to $25.50 in early trading on the NYSE.
